_about: Victorian election model (.build/analysis/seat-model/vic-simulate.mjs): 20,000 simulated elections for Saturday 28 November 2026, 88 Assembly seats. The federal 2028 model's engine on Victoria's base: the /vic/ polling average; the VEC's 734 nominated candidates, each starting from its party's or its own 2022 vote in the district (One Nation: its federal 2025 footprint; a party with no 2022 Assembly vote there: its 2022 Council vote; a candidate new to the ballot: the 2022 median); sitting-member terms, polling error and district noise fitted on state elections; preferences from the 2025 Senate ballots at the nearest federal polling place (House-calibrated), the Greens' and minor parties' Labor-v-Coalition levels set to Victoria's 2022 count, every level involving One Nation moved halfway from the federal reading to Victorian poll respondents' own allocation, and the registered how-to-vote cards read district by district. HARD LIMITS: no age/gender term; by-elections since 2022 change who sits, not the starting vote; candidates disendorsed after nominations closed are counted as their party's; the Legislative Council is not modelled.
